source.title: LoGo: Token-Level Dynamic Local-Global Attention
source.authors: Yu-Qi Pan; Zheng Li; Bo-Hao Tang; Zhen Qin; Guoqi Li

record.tranche_reason: The study runs a model-size sweep and reports language-modeling and downstream results, but does not fit or test the power-law relations or extrapolations in the claim.
record.gate_note: Section 4.1 and Table 1 report losses, perplexities, and downstream accuracy across five model sizes. The losses and perplexities are scaling outcomes, but the paper does not fit power laws to them; training loss is not held-out pretraining loss, and WikiText and Lambada perplexities are not pretraining loss. Only the commonsense-reasoning averages are linked to V6. The fixed tokens-per-parameter recipe is not a test of compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The scaling sweep (Sec 4.1, Table 1) checks whether the authors' LoGo attention 'preserves Transformer scaling behavior' next to a full-attention baseline. It uses Chinchilla's 20 tokens-per-parameter recipe as a fixed setting. It fits no power law, makes no extrapolation or prediction, and does no allocation sweep or shape comparison. The five sizes span about 1.2 orders of magnitude. The reported result is the method's performance against its baseline, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude LoGo preserves Transformer scaling and matches or improves it at every size, but per-size differences are small (e.g. train loss 0.004-0.012). LoGo's CSR-Avg is slightly lower at 1.5B (52.68 vs 52.88), and no uncertainty is reported. Their main claims concern the long-context performance-compute trade-off and gains on long-range retrieval.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a model-size sweep with a fixed tokens-per-parameter ratio and compares LoGo with full attention; it does not fit the original scaling laws or perform their extrapolation procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: For both Transformer and LoGo at TPP 20, train loss, WikiText and Lambada perplexity fall, and CSR-Avg rises, monotonically from 200M to 3.3B parameters (e.g. Transformer CSR 38.89 to 58.11). No fit is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under a fixed 20 tokens-per-parameter recipe, loss and average zero-shot commonsense accuracy improve monotonically with model size from 200M to 3.3B, for both full and dynamic local-global attention.

record.problems: The scaling sweep covers five sizes from 200M to 3.3B with a fixed tokens-per-parameter ratio, so parameters, tokens, and compute are not independently tested. No power-law fits, extrapolation checks, or uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: No power-law fit. Train loss only, at fixed TPP. About 1.2 orders of magnitude in parameters.
TPP fixed at 20 by assumption. No fixed-compute allocation sweep.
Depth and width vary with size (Table 6) but never at a fixed parameter count.
Only CSR averages that rise monotonically. No fitted or predicted downstream trend, and no loss-to-task mapping.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: All rows' baselines are the other architecture at the same size, i.e. method-versus-method comparisons rather than scale baselines. The reader's states ('observed' meaning lower than the previous size) mix the two framings. The scale trend is real but untested against any power law or prediction. The architecture also changes with size (layers 12 to 32), and the batch size changes at 3.3B.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit is reported; training loss is not held-out pretraining loss, and tokens and compute are not varied independently.
No predictions from small runs or comparisons with larger runs are reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or fitted parameter/token growth trends are reported.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
No other modality or training regime is tested.
Reports only average commonsense-reasoning accuracy across scales, not individual downstream-task trends or predictions from pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or curve shapes is reported.
